stem: The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) learns of a possible violation of a person's civil and political rights, but no one has filed a complaint. Under Article XIII, Section 18 of the 1987 Constitution, may the CHR investigate?
choices: No. It must wait for a complaint from the victim.
No. It needs an order from the President first.
Only if Congress asks it to look into the case.
Yes. It may investigate on its own.
answer: Yes. It may investigate on its own.
hints: Look at how the first power in Section 18 begins. It says who can start an investigation.
Recall the opening words of Section 18(1): the CHR may investigate "on its own or on complaint by any party".
With "or", either way is enough to start. Check which choices add a condition that the text does not have.

solution.methodName: Recall the exact words of the provision

steps.action: Find the provision: Article XIII, Section 18(1) of the 1987 Constitution.
Read it: the CHR may "Investigate, on its own or on complaint by any party, all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights".
The word "or" gives two separate ways to start: on its own, or on a complaint.
steps.why: With "or", either one is enough. A complaint is not required.

steps.action: Section 18(1) does not ask for the President's order or for a request from Congress.
steps.why: Section 17 creates the CHR as "an independent office".

steps.action: The answer is: yes, it may investigate on its own.

trapNotes.No. It must wait for a complaint from th: Section 18(1) says the CHR may investigate "on its own or on complaint by any party". A complaint is one way to start, not the only way.
trapNotes.No. It needs an order from the President: Section 17 creates the CHR as "an independent office", and Section 18(1) does not require the President's order.
trapNotes.Only if Congress asks it to look into th: Section 19 lets Congress add other kinds of cases to the CHR's authority, but Section 18(1) does not require Congress to ask before the CHR investigates.
